summary: Isabel Savory’s account of a long stay in India that began in January 1898 (the year is inferred from the total eclipse of the sun she watched soon after landing), much of it spent hunting with companions named only by initials. She landed at Bombay, saw the Taj Mahal, and rode after wild boar near Lahore; visited Peshawar and rode through the Khyber Pass; went up to Dalhousie and into Chamba after bear and tahr; travelled on into Kashmir, where she climbed above the snow line, lived in a house-boat at Srinagar, and shot black bears; and went on a tiger shoot in the Deccan. Later chapters describe snakes, Delhi and the Mutiny sites, Ootacamund and the Todas, an elephant kheddah in Mysore, crocodile tanks, and letters written in Indian English, and end with her thoughts on travel. Hunting is described in detail. The book has a portrait of the author and 48 plates from photographs and drawings.
